checks.scope: Only BRIEF-6.md Part A: crater-prop-0 through crater-prop-7. Approved files and reference/ art were used for calibration only and were not assigned verdicts.
checks.prior_review: critic-r6A-0.json does not exist; no inherited pass decisions apply.
checks.individual_8x: Every Part A file visually inspected at nearest-neighbour 8x: 0-3 over approved grass and snow; 4-7 on checker. Additional light, dark, checker and grass/snow enlargements are saved for every file. Pixel clusters remain deliberate. Partial alpha is required shading, not evidence by itself of unwanted anti-aliasing. No blur, fringe, matte or stray noisy contour warrants rejection.
checks.dimensions_and_placement: 0-3 are 48x48 and 4-7 are 96x96. Visible bounding boxes are centred to within 2.5px of the sprite centre. Transparent padding fully surrounds each scar. Mixed-size composites test cell-centred placement, jitter, overlap and large-sprite spill beyond a 48px cell at 1x and 4x. Clipping at the outside of the test viewport is not in the source files.
checks.neutral_alpha: All visible pixels have R=G=B; no baked-in ground hue. Every visible pixel is partially transparent. Maximum black alpha is 166/255 (65.1%); maximum white alpha is 115/255 (45.1%), within the brief's approximate limits. Every image border is alpha zero. Numerical per-file evidence is in critic-r6A-1-audit.json.
checks.edges_and_light: Viewed over green, pale snow, textured brown dirt and flat tan sand at 1x/4x. Broken upper-left outer-rim glints remain consistent with the approved top-left light. Dark upper interior walls are compatible with concave bowls. Stepped faint ejecta fades into clear ground; no continuous outline, square edge or light fringe appears.
checks.random_8x2: 0-3 inspected in a seeded 8x2 random arrangement on approved grass and snow at 1x and 4x. Each appears four times, shuffled independently by row. There is no tile border or square backdrop. Individual motifs can of course be recognised when deliberately repeated, but their silhouettes differ enough that the set does not collapse into one identical hole stamp.
checks.shape_and_noise: Uneven, angular blast scars rather than clean lunar circles. Ash streaks follow the scars, and sparse detached pixels read as local ejecta/rubble rather than evenly distributed dither. 3 and 7 are the two clusters. Larger jittered scatter viewed at 1x and 4x on grass and snow does not turn the ground into regular Swiss-cheese rings.
checks.ground_and_seasons: All eight inspected together at 1x/4x on approved summer/spring grass, summer/autumn plains, winter grass, textured wasteland dirt and a flat sand-colour control. Shared props retain underlying hue, with appropriate grey scars on snow. Part A requires no seasonal copies; winter is tested by compositing the same files, and is neither blank nor geometrically inconsistent.
checks.approved_art: Compared with all six settings' approved markers; round-2 city/slums/industry/suburb/farmland/farmstead examples; paddies; all seasonal grass/plains bases and selected details. Summer and winter context scenes inspected at 1x and 4x. The quiet unoutlined terrain shading sits beside the more strongly outlined standing art without adding a foreign palette or incompatible pixel density.
checks.near_duplicates: 0 and 2 share a small-bowl role but differ in width, rim shape, right notch and interior mass. 1 is elongated. Large 4 is radial, 5 diagonal and 6 broad with a sideward blast. Clusters 3 and 7 differ in pit count, scale and arrangement. No pair warrants rejection as a near-duplicate.
checks.not_applicable: Part A contains no seamless bases, peaks/ridges, trees, ruins or cyberpunk tiles. Therefore 3x3 base tiling, peak lattice/range, forest composites, egg-crate peaks, classical ruins, stamped cyberpunk streets, flat orange foliage and identical crowns do not apply. No files from Parts B-E were reviewed.

file_observations.crater-prop-0: PASS. Broad, low diamond-shaped bowl with a broken upper rim, off-centre dark pocket and short rightward ejecta. At 1x its shallow bowl remains readable on grass and snow. The compact, higher-backed shape of 2 is visibly different; these are not duplicate stamps.
file_observations.crater-prop-1: PASS. Narrow southwest-to-northeast gouge with a long torn upper-right extension. The sloping ash band and uneven rim distinguish it from the broad bowls. Small upper-left rim glints agree with the common light direction; the extension is ejecta, not a reversed highlight.
file_observations.crater-prop-2: PASS. Compact bowl with a pointed back, steep dark interior and a conspicuous open notch on the right. Its narrow upright silhouette and missing right rim distinguish it from 0. No smooth circular ring or clipped edge.
file_observations.crater-prop-3: PASS. First cluster: a principal pit with two separated satellite pits, in an asymmetric triangle. All three survive native-size viewing, including on snow. The clear ground between pits and restrained rubble avoid a Swiss-cheese ground pattern.
file_observations.crater-prop-4: PASS. Broad large blast bowl with uneven northern rim spurs and diagonal ash/ejecta through the lower-right half. Its large dark centre is an intentional bowl; the rim and streaks keep it readable rather than a featureless blot. Irregular pixel-stepped fading contains no rectangular matte.
file_observations.crater-prop-5: PASS. Long diagonal scar with a torn tall northeast end and a tapering southwest end. The split ash streak and narrow footprint distinguish it from both broad large scars. The neutral overlay keeps dirt, sand and grass hues visible through the shading.
file_observations.crater-prop-6: PASS. Wide, squat scar with an indented right edge and long right/lower-right ejecta. Its silhouette, sideward throw and crossed ash bands distinguish it from the rounder radial bowl 4 and diagonal gouge 5. No cell-edge cutoff or uniform white halo.
file_observations.crater-prop-7: PASS. Second cluster: two medium pits and three smaller satellites, separated by visible ground and sparse linking ash. This is a different arrangement from 3, not an enlarged copy. At native size the pits remain separate, and winter retains the same readable geometry.
